request: Check this flight: did a control fault occur, when, and where on the aircraft?

result.headline: Throttle output ch[2] cut to minimum at t=103-104 s and stayed there; aircraft lost altitude until end of log.
result.explanation: Propulsion command collapsed from 70% to 0% while attitude demands continued. Trigger cannot be separated: battery undervoltage cutoff, throttle/ESC output fault, or a commanded cut. The t=1.3 s battery and sensor warnings are unresolved.

evidence.shows: Throttle falls from 70% (t=102) to 0% in one second and stays 0 to t=124, while ch[2] was still 1670 us.
ch[2] drops to 1100 us (minimum) at t=104 and stays pinned to t=124. ch[2] tracks throttle throughout (about 1130 us at 4%, about 1660 us at 70%).
Altitude falls from about 51 m (t=106) to 17.6 m at the end of the log. Pitch setpoint is held at +17 deg and ch[1] has saturated at 1100 us since t=119.

checked.check: Compared ch[2] with throttle over the whole flight
checked.result: ch[2] follows throttle closely until t=103, then both stay at the minimum value.

checked.check: Looked for a pre-fault drift on any actuator channel
checked.result: No gradual trend before t=103. The cut is abrupt and the earlier roll/throttle cycling is repetitive and similar before and after.

checked.check: Looked at airspeed and the t=1.3 s events
checked.result: Airspeed reads 0 for the whole flight, which is consistent with the 'Sensor helth' error. The Low voltage warning appears only at t=1.3 s and is not repeated at t=103.

effects.shows: ch[1] saturates at minimum as the controller fights roll and pitch demands without thrust.

effects.why: Altitude loss follows from the loss of thrust.

next_action.action: Pull full-rate logs around t=100-106 s for ESC, battery and throttle command
next_action.why: Separates undervoltage cutoff from an output or ESC fault and from a commanded cut.
how: Check battery voltage and current at 100-104 s
Check the throttle command against actuator.output[ch2]
Check the failsafe and mode log at t=103

outcomes.label: Battery voltage collapsed at t=103
outcomes.then: Inspect the pack and replace or test it

outcomes.label: Voltage normal, command stayed high
outcomes.means: Output or ESC fault on ch[2].
outcomes.then: Bench test ESC and motor on ch[2]

unknowns: Why throttle went to 0 at t=103
What the Low voltage and Sensor health warnings at t=1.3 s refer to

hypotheses.claim: Propulsion output channel ch[2] failed or was cut to minimum at t=103-104.
hypotheses.because: Abrupt 70% to 0% with the output pinned at 1100 us, while attitude setpoints still demand activity.

hypotheses.claim: Low battery voltage triggered a motor cutoff or failsafe.
hypotheses.because: A Low voltage warning was logged at t=1.3 s, but there is no voltage signal to confirm it at t=103.

hypotheses.claim: Airspeed sensor fault (reads 0 all flight) contributed to the cut.
hypotheses.because: It was 0 for the entire flight, including the normal period before t=103.

events.what: Throttle drops to 0 and ch[2] pinned at 1100 us
Low voltage and Sensor health warnings at 1.3 s
events.why: Early warnings; the flight continued normally for 100 s
Response to attitude demands without thrust
